question.text: A projectile is fired from horizontal ground with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> and projection angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math>. When the acceleration due to gravity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi></math>, the range of the projectile is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math>. If at the highest point in its trajectory, the projectile enters a different region where the effective acceleration due to gravity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>g</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>81</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>, then the new range is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Horizontal range of the projectile is d=v2sin2θg

Maximum height attained by the projectile is H=v2sin2θ2g

So, after entering the new region, time taken by projectile to reach ground

t=2Hg'=2v2sin2θ2gg0.81

=0.94vsinθg

So, horizontal displacement done by the projectile in new region is

x=0.9vsinθg×vcosθ

=0.9v2sin2θ2g

So, new range is d'=d2+x

=v2sin2θ2g+0.9v2sin2θ2g

=0.95 d

So, n=0.95 d
